topic: Autonomous Resolver opened false-positive workflow-failure issues from failed PR-branch YAML validation runs

main_workflow.current_main_behavior: Hourly schedule; contents:read, issues:write and pull-requests:write; scans failed workflow runs and may create public issues, then optionally assign unassigned issues and PRs.

root_cause.description: The workflow comment says it scans failures from the last 24 hours, but the gh run list command uses --status failure --limit 100 and does not pass --created, --branch main or an event filter. It aggregates distinct workflow names from failed runs across branches. For each name, a second gh run list --workflow NAME --status failure --limit 1 also lacks a branch/event filter. Consequently a failed pull-request validation run can be treated as a main-branch operational failure and create a public issue.
root_cause.evidence_from_main_source: .github/workflows/barrot-autonomous-resolver.yml was retrieved from main c10df289. The query contains --status failure and --limit 100; no time, branch or event filter is present.
root_cause.additional_risk: The body says 'most recent failed run', not 'latest run overall'. A later successful run does not prevent issue creation if an older failure remains in the returned set.

correction_history.earlier_issue: The first quarantine revision used plain scalar run: echo text containing colon-space, which caused YAML parsing to fail before jobs were created.
correction_history.observed_effect: All six referenced runs have zero jobs and were push events on the PR branch, not main scheduled executions.
correction_history.corrected_validation: PR #1573 later passed exact-head CI with 345 tests plus 8 subtests and its fail-closed gate. This proves the corrected PR head passed its suite; it does not change the earlier failed-run history.

assignment_behavior.evidence: The resolver job log printed 'No COPILOT_ASSIGNEE repository variable configured; skipping issue assignment' and the equivalent message for pull requests.

related_auto_resolve_workflow.main_behavior: Daily schedule, issues:write, runs scripts/resolve_issue.py --all. The script comments and closes matching issues when the latest run for a workflow succeeds, without a per-issue human approval step.
related_auto_resolve_workflow.risk: The six newly created issues are not necessarily safe for automated closure. They should be reviewed against their exact branch/event evidence; do not infer that a workflow is fixed or was broken on main from these issue titles alone.
related_auto_resolve_workflow.containment: PR #1573 replaces this workflow with a manual-only disabled job and permissions: {}.

remediation.immediate: Keep the resolver quarantined pending review; do not automatically close issues #1574-#1579.
future_safe_reenablement_requirements: Filter runs to the default branch and approved event types.
Apply an explicit --created cutoff matching the stated window.
For each workflow, inspect the latest completed run overall on main; create an issue only if that latest run failed.
Record workflow ID, run ID, branch, event, head SHA, created_at and conclusion in the issue body.
Deduplicate by workflow ID plus default-branch failure episode, not only display name.
Use a bounded issue-creation limit and idempotency key.
Do not auto-assign unless an explicit reviewed assignee is configured.
Keep automatic issue closure disabled until each issue has a separate approval boundary and auditable resolution evidence.
Add tests with PR-branch failure followed by main success, stale failure, cancelled run and same-name workflow cases.

next_actions: Retain PR #1573 as the quarantine candidate; its current head is 42520c0b7ac7036c2a49f4abc4b5f0d458ba5289.
Review the six false-positive issues manually before any closure.
If the user later authorizes re-enablement, implement and test branch/event/time/latest-run filtering in a separate reviewed change.
Keep main unchanged until the user authorizes the security PR.
safety: No issue was edited or closed; no workflow was dispatched; no credentials or subscriber/corpus records were accessed; no main-branch mutation was performed.
